concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Who decided to go ahead with his plans of invasion of Afghanistan resulting in the first Anglo-Afghan War?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Auckland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first Anglo-Afghan War** took place from **1839 to 1842**.
 
• It was one of the first major conflicts during the "Great Game," the 19th-century competition for **power and influence in Central Asia between the United Kingdom and Russia**.
 
• The **decision to invade Afghanistan was made by George Eden, Earl of Auckland,** also known as Lord Auckland.
 
• He was serving as **Governor-General of India at the time**. Lord Auckland's proclamation issuing the invasion, often referred to as the **"Simla Manifesto",** was issued on October 1, 1838.
 
• His plans for the invasion were prompted by fears of growing Russian influence in Afghanistan and threats to India, then a part of the British Empire.
 
• Auckland's strategy was to replace the existing ruler, Dost Mohammad Khan, with a pro-British monarch, Shah Shuja.
 
• This plan ultimately ended in failure and backlash, leading to what is often considered one of the greatest military humiliations of the British Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Edward Law, Earl of Ellenborough, replaced Lord Auckland as Governor-General of India and it fell upon him to resolve the debacle of the First Anglo-Afghan War.
 
• James Ramsay, Earl of Dalhousie, served much later and was Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. He is known for his policy of annexation, the doctrine of lapse, and for introducing railways and telegraph to India.
 
• Edward Robert Bulwer-Lytton, served as the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880. His tenure is known for the controversial Vernacular Press Act and the controversial handling of the Great Famine of 1876–78.
